scope: AirIndia / EGY full regression on stg-ne-3: TestCases_Generic.csv + TestCases_V1.csv + TestCases_V2.csv + SeatMap_TestCases.csv + new AirIndia exploratory rows
title_line: AirIndia / EGY - Full Regression - stg-ne-3 - V1 and V2 - 484 test cases
scope_text: Generic CSV (64 rows) + V1 CSV (59 rows) + V2 CSV (212 rows) + SeatMap CSV (68 rows), each executed or recorded BLOCKED with the reason, plus 85 new AirIndia/EGY rows (request validation, auth, error envelope, ID-chain negatives on 16 endpoints, passenger limits, isdebug exposure, capability gate). Flows written for other suppliers are re-targeted to AirIndia/EGY.
description_text: Full regression of the AirIndia supplier on the EGY credentials against the stg-ne-3 staging build, V1 and V2, with emphasis on happy scenarios and end-to-end flows. AirIndia returns no bookable inventory on this build, so every flow is BLOCKED and the run concentrates on what can be verified without offers.

title: [FC-SM-A][Response] Verify Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap -> FareCheck* -> Book -> Retrieve completes with a booked/confirmed bookingStatus at the final Retrieve, matching Book's selectedOffer/price; and the chosen seat cellCode correctly reflected as a priced Seat-category line.
expected: Per-family state check (SPEC.md 6.3, Family A): bookingStatus reads a booked/confirmed state at the final Retrieve, with selectedOffer.offerId/priceDetails.totalAmount matching between Book and Retrieve. Per-enrichment state check(s) (SPEC.md 6.4): the chosen GetSeatMap cellCode appears as a Seat-category entry in passengersSelectedAncillaries, priced per what GetSeatMap/FareCheck reported for that cell; the final booking price equals FareCheck's re-priced total (not the pre-ancillary FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era total) -- the highest-value price-integrity assertion for this enrichment. FareCheck conditionality: FareCheck must actually run only if the immediately-preceding GetAncillary/GetSeatMap response reported isFareCheckRequired=true; do not treat FareCheck as unconditionally present, and if it is required, the price delta between the pre-FareCheck and post-FareCheck totals should equal the sum of the selected ancillary/seat prices (2.8). Manual price-reconciliation requirement (V2 script coverage gap, SPEC.md 1.4/2.1/6.2/7.10): per passenger type, sum(taxesAndFees[].amount.amount) == paxTotalTaxAmount.amount, and totals reconcile per the Section 2.1 formula; this is enforced by script at Hold/FareConfirmAfterHold/BookAfterHold in V2, but NOT at Search/FareConfirm/Book/Retrieve -- the tester must supply this check manually at every Book/Retrieve step in this flow. Assert the GetSeatMap-selected cellCode was correctly hand-carried into Book/Hold's PassengersSelectedAncillaries; a mismatched or omitted cellCode is the single most likely manual-execution error in flows 49-72.

title: [FC-BDL+ANC+SM-A][Response] Verify Search -> FareConfirm -> GetOfferBundles -> AddPassenger -> GetAncillary -> GetSeatMap -> FareCheck* -> Book -> Retrieve completes with a booked/confirmed bookingStatus at the final Retrieve, matching Book's selectedOffer/price; and bundle pricing correctly reflected without double-charging included services; selected ancillaries correctly reflected in passengersSelectedAncillaries/paxTotalAncillaryAmount; the chosen seat cellCode correctly reflected as a priced Seat-category line.
expected: Per-family state check (SPEC.md 6.3, Family A): bookingStatus reads a booked/confirmed state at the final Retrieve, with selectedOffer.offerId/priceDetails.totalAmount matching between Book and Retrieve. Per-enrichment state check(s) (SPEC.md 6.4): the booking's final priceDetails.totalAmount reflects the selected bundle's feePrice added to the base offer price, and any bundle-included service (baggage/seat/meal per includedServices tags) does NOT also appear as a separately-priced ancillary line; passengersSelectedAncillaries on Book/Hold/Retrieve lists exactly the ancillary codes selected at GetAncillary/FareCheck time with matching AdditionalServiceCategory/quantity, and paxTotalAncillaryAmount equals the sum of the selected ancillaries' prices; the chosen GetSeatMap cellCode appears as a Seat-category entry in passengersSelectedAncillaries, priced per what GetSeatMap/FareCheck reported for that cell; the final booking price equals FareCheck's re-priced total (not the pre-ancillary FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era total) -- the highest-value price-integrity assertion for this enrichment. Assert the GetSeatMap-selected cellCode was correctly hand-carried into Book/Hold's PassengersSelectedAncillaries; a mismatched or omitted cellCode is the single most likely manual-execution error in flows 49-72.

Per-enrichment state check(s) (SPEC.md 6.4): the booking's final priceDetails.totalAmount reflects the selected bundle's feePrice added to the base offer price, and any bundle-included service (baggage/seat/meal per includedServices tags) does NOT also appear as a separately-priced ancillary line; passengersSelectedAncillaries on Book/Hold/Retrieve lists exactly the ancillary codes selected at GetAncillary/FareCheck time with matching AdditionalServiceCategory/quantity, and paxTotalAncillaryAmount equals the sum of the selected ancillaries' prices; the chosen GetSeatMap cellCode appears as a Seat-category entry in passengersSelectedAncillaries, priced per what GetSeatMap/FareCheck reported for that cell; the final booking price equals FareCheck's re-priced total (not the pre-ancillary FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era total) -- the highest-value price-integrity assertion for this enrichment. FareCheck conditionality: FareCheck must actually run only if the immediately-preceding GetAncillary/GetSeatMap response reported isFareCheckRequired=true; do not treat FareCheck as unconditionally present, and if it is required, the price delta between the pre-FareCheck and post-FareCheck totals should equal the sum of the selected ancillary/seat prices (2.8). Manual price-reconciliation requirement (V2 script coverage gap, SPEC.md 1.4/2.1/6.2/7.10): per passenger type, sum(taxesAndFees[].amount.amount) == paxTotalTaxAmount.amount, and totals reconcile per the Section 2.1 formula; this is enforced by script at Hold/FareConfirmAfterHold/BookAfterHold in V2, but NOT at Search/FareConfirm/Book/Retrieve -- the tester must supply this check manually at every Book/Retrieve step in this flow. Assert passengersAncillariesAvailabilty (GetAncillary response) is spelled exactly as the live API returns it -- missing the second "i" -- since this is a genuine API field-name defect, not a documentation typo. Assert the GetSeatMap-selected cellCode was correctly hand-carried into Book/Hold's PassengersSelectedAncillaries; a mismatched or omitted cellCode is the single most likely manual-execution error in flows 49-72.
actual: Not executable on AirIndia: the chain needs Hold / BookAfterHold / FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) / Void / CancelAfterHold / Upselling / FareCheck / FareRules / SeatAfterHold, which AirIndia does not support (live: 409 OperationNotSupported on V1 and V2, see the TC-AIEGY-*-NEG-01 cases for each endpoint; supplier matrix lists them N/A). Independently, no inventory is returned (TC-AIEGY-CAP-01).

summary: V1 FareConfirm does not validate the search id locally: a never-issued or wrongly named id (ResponseId instead of searchResponseId) is forwarded to the supplier and the call hangs about 135 s before returning 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 "Connection timed out". V1 and V2 Retrieve of an unknown PNR hang the same ~135 s. V2 FareConfirm rejects the same input in 0.4 s with 400 "selected offer is invalid"
expected_value: 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 within about a second ("selected offer is invalid, expired or could not be found"), as V2 FareConfirm does; Retrieve of an unknown PNR returns a mapped not-found error
impact: A bad id ties up a request thread for over two minutes and surfaces as an unmapped Z9999; clients will time out first
evidence: TC-FARECONFIRM-VAL-01 (V1 134.7 s), TC-AIEGY-FARECONFIRM-NEG-01 (V1 135.9 s), TC-AIEGY-RETRIEVE-NEG-01 (V1 137.1 s, V2 135.3 s), TC-AIEGY-SEC-02

field_name: V1 Book and V1 GetOfferBundles (unknown or missing id)
summary: V1 Book and V1 GetOfferBundles return HTTP 500 ServerError ("Unknown error occured") for a never-issued fareConfirmResponseId/selectedOfferId pair, for a missing fareConfirmResponseId and for a 1000-character selectedOfferId, where V2 Book and V2 GetOfferBundles return 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001
expected_value: 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 "selected offer is invalid, expired or could not be found" (the V2 behaviour)
impact: A bad id on the booking path looks like a platform outage; support cannot tell caller error from server fault
evidence: TC-AIEGY-BOOK-NEG-01, TC-AIEGY-BOOK-NEG-03, TC-BOOK-NEG-12, TC-BOOK-VAL-01, TC-BOOK-VAL-02, TC-AIEGY-GETOFFERBUNDLES-NEG-01/02/03, TC-AIEGY-CHAIN-02

summary: Search accepts a party of one child with no adult (CHD 1) and a party of 10 that is over the 9-passenger limit only because of infants (6 ADT + 2 CHD + 2 INF); both return HTTP 200 on V1 and V2, while 10 seated passengers, an infant alone and more infants than adults are rejected with 400
expected_value: 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 for both parties (an adult is required; the 9-passenger cap counts infants)
impact: Invalid parties reach the supplier (and cost a 15 s supplier round trip) and would fail later at Book
evidence: TC-AIEGY-SRCH-PAX-03 (CHD only), TC-AIEGY-SRCH-PAX-06 (10 with infants)

summary: Client errors use two different envelopes: model-binding validation failures return camelCase {status, errorCode "1001", errorMessage, context[], originalSupplierRequest: null} while business validation and auth use PascalCase {Status, ErrorCode "NDC-INT-TEC-A0001" / "AuthenticationError" / "OperationNotSupported" / "NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999"}. Over 570 4xx responses: about 300 camelCase vs 260 PascalCase
expected_value: One envelope with one casing, for example {"Status":400,"TransactionId":"...","ErrorCode":"NDC-INT-TEC-A0001","ErrorMessage":"...","Context":[...]} for every client error
impact: Clients need two parsers; error-code mapping breaks silently
evidence: TC-VERSIONDIFF-NEG-01 (Search, FareConfirm and Book differ by cause), TC-AIEGY-ENV-01 (census)

summary: Validation errors expose internal implementation detail: .NET type names (System.DateTime, System.Guid, System.Int32, NDC.Integrations.Application.Dtos.Api.Supplier), JSON path with line and byte position, and the exception class name SocketException. A bad supplier value also returns the misleading text "The airSearchRequestDto field is required." although the DTO is present
expected_value: A neutral message naming the field, for example "supplier must be one of the supported suppliers", with no type names or parser positions
impact: Information disclosure that helps an attacker fingerprint the stack; misleading messages slow integrators down
evidence: TC-AIEGY-SEC-LEAK-01: about 126 of 666 captured responses contain such detail

field_name: Search error code for unsupported multi-city
summary: The same unsupported multi-city Search ("The supplier does not support multi city searches") returns HTTP 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 on V1 but HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (the unmapped catch-all code) on V2
expected_value: The same status and mapped ErrorCode on both versions (400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001)
impact: V2 callers cannot distinguish a known business limitation from an unknown supplier failure
evidence: TC-AIEGY-EXP-01, TC-AIEGY-SRCH-SC-09

summary: Hold, BookAfterHold, PnrReprice, CancelAfterHold, Void, Upselling, FareCheck, FareRules and SeatAfterHold reject AirIndia with 409 OperationNotSupported and the context text "AirIndia does not exists" on V1 and V2, before any id is looked at. The unsupported-operation behaviour matches the supplier matrix (N/A) but the message reads like a missing-supplier registration error
expected_value: 409 OperationNotSupported with a message such as "Hold is not supported for supplier AirIndia"
impact: Integrators and support read it as a configuration fault and may open false incidents; it also hides whether the supplier name is mapped correctly (compare the Indigo / ElJazeera name-mismatch bug in SPEC 4.5)
evidence: TC-AIEGY-UPSELLING/HOLD/PNRREPRICE/BOOKAFTERHOLD/CANCELAFTERHOLD/VOID/FARECHECK/FARERULES/SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-01

summary: AirIndia credential selectors on ne-3: EGY is active; UAE and KSA return 400 "The credentials for the selected supplier do not exist or are not active" with the same text on V1 and V2. Supplier name and selector matching ignore case and surrounding whitespace (airindia, AIRINDIA, " AirIndia", egy, "EGY " all accepted)
evidence: TC-AIEGY-CAP-03, TC-AIEGY-SRCH-SUP-03, TC-AIEGY-SRCH-CRED-03 (2026-11-02)

summary: Live AirIndia capability on ne-3 (V1 and V2): Hold, BookAfterHold, FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice), CancelAfterHold, Void, Upselling, FareCheck and FareRules are not supported (409 OperationNotSupported); SeatAfterHold likewise. FareConfirm, AddPassenger, GetAncillary, GetSeatMap, Book, GetOfferBundles and Retrieve are routed (id lookup reached). So only terminal Family A (Book then Retrieve) can ever run for AirIndia; Families B-F (Hold, Void, Cancel) cannot
evidence: The nine TC-AIEGY-*-NEG-01 cases; supplier matrix lists the same endpoints N/A

summary: Error baseline observed on ne-3: 400 camelCase code 1001 (model binding), 400 PascalCase NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 (business validation, inactive credentials, offer not found), 401 AuthenticationError ("Invalid authorization header") for an altered or missing x-api-key and for an altered Client-Id, 405 for GET/PUT/DELETE on Search, 409 OperationNotSupported, 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (supplier timeout, multi-city on V2), 500 ServerError (V1 Book and V1 GetOfferBundles with unknown ids)
evidence: TC-VERSIONDIFF-NEG-01/02, TC-AIEGY-ENV-01, TC-AUTH-SEC-01/02, TC-AIEGY-SRCH-HTTP-01

summary: Search does not validate that an IATA code exists or is upper case: origin XXX and del return 200 with an empty offers[] on V1 and V2. A departure date of today or 2028-12-01, an unknown preferredAirlines value (XX), an extra unknown body field and a 2 MB body are all accepted (200). Duplicate segments and multi-city are rejected with 400
evidence: TC-SEARCH-NEG-03, TC-AIEGY-SRCH-SC-07/SC-09, TC-AIEGY-SRCH-BODY-04/05, TC-AIEGY-EXP-04

new_text: | AirIndia | Unknown (GetOfferBundles reachable; no offers to test) | Not Supported (Upselling 409 OperationNotSupported, V1+V2, 2026-11-02) | Not Supported (CancelAfterHold 409) | Not Supported (Void 409) | Not Supported (Hold 409; matches the supplier matrix N/A) | Unknown (GetAncillary reachable; no offers to test) | Unknown (GetSeatMap reachable; the supplier matrix says N/A) |

text: Run of 484 test cases against supplier AirIndia, credentialsSelector EGY, staging stg-ne-3 (V1 and V2): 89 pass, 23 fail, 372 blocked. Sources: TestCases_Generic.csv (64), TestCases_V1.csv (59), TestCases_V2.csv (212), SeatMap_TestCases.csv (68; shared IDs get a suffix) plus 86 new AirIndia rows (AirIndia_EGY_Regression_TestCases.csv). AirIndia returned no inventory on any of 1,618 route/date searches, so no booking, hold, ticket or PNR was created and no cleanup is needed. Every row that needs an offer is BLOCKED, with the reason on the row; rows whose chain needs Hold, Void, Cancel, Upselling, FareCheck, FareRules or SeatAfterHold are marked not executable on AirIndia. Nothing was sent to any other supplier.
